Said on [hypodrafts/B1.md](hypodrafts/B1.md).

<a id="C-BA-B1-NOT-OXYGEN"></a>
### It would say nothing about oxygen: this is [B1](hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow")'s delivery limb, bearing on [O9](HYPOTHESES.md "Bathing water failure"), not [O1](HYPOTHESES.md "Oxygen deficit"); faecal indicators are not oxygen demand, and they are not the rotting algae that fedtemøg names, so [O2](HYPOTHESES.md "Fedtemøg") stays unscored too.

`C-BA-B1-NOT-OXYGEN` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/B1.md](hypodrafts/B1.md).

**Why it follows:** The register lists those outcomes for the hypothesis; a faecal count measures contamination, not oxygen or algae, and fedtemøg is loose filamentous brown algae.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-BA-OLD-B1-O2): Fedtemøg names rotting filamentous algae, which a faecal count does not measure, so the test does not bear on that outcome even weakly.

<a id="C-AF-C1-CIRC2"></a>
### Salinity is computed from conductivity and temperature, so φ rests on two sensor channels and oxygen on a third: not circular, but φ's error and the bed temperature's error are correlated wherever bed temperature is a covariate.

`C-AF-C1-CIRC2` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C1.md](hypodrafts/C1.md).

**Why it follows:** The national CTD method uses conductivity only to compute salinity, which it determines from conductivity and temperature; an error in temperature therefore enters φ twice.


<a id="C-AF-C1-CIRC3"></a>
### The residual coupling is thermodynamic: oxygen solubility falls as temperature rises and depends on salinity, so a warm stratified summer has high φ and low saturation concentration for reasons that are [C6](hypodrafts/C6.md "Water temperature and solubility"), not [C1](hypodrafts/C1.md "Stratification strength"); no covariate removes it, so it is measured, by Null A.

`C-AF-C1-CIRC3` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C1.md](hypodrafts/C1.md).

**Why it follows:** DCE's note says higher temperature lowers oxygen solubility; the NOVA method computes saturation with temperature and salinity. A covariate cannot separate a quantity from a deterministic function of the same inputs; a surrogate can be computed and compared.

<a id="C-CC-C4-ORDER"></a>
### The falsifiable half of [C4](hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") is ordered propagation: a wind-forced inflow event produces a bottom-salinity anomaly whose peak lag increases along the path Belts/Øresund, Arkona, Bornholm, Gotland Deep, read there at [200](SOURCES.md#F-9be4156372) m; the test is whether the peaks fall in that order.

`C-CC-C4-ORDER` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** [C4](hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") has dense saline pulses pass through the Belts into the deep basins, so water entering at the straits reaches the basins further along the path later: the order of arrival is fixed by the hypothesis before any fit. The Gotland depth is the one the published inflow statistics read the eastern Gotland Basin at.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C4-WINDOWS): The windows were derived from a travel distance and a speed that no source held or pinned here gives, so they rested on a physical claim without support. The ordering test does not need them.

<a id="C-CC-C4-SECONDARY"></a>
### An event should raise near-bed salinity more than surface salinity; if both rise alike, the salinity difference between bed and surface at the Danish stations does not grow, and the part of [C4](hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") that has the pulses strengthen stratification is not seen at the Danish end.

`C-CC-C4-SECONDARY` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** Stratification in these waters sits at the halocline, a salinity difference between deep and surface water; a rise shared by bed and surface leaves that difference, and so the stratification, unchanged.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C4-BAROTROPIC): Nothing held or pinned here says a barotropic exchange leaves stratification unchanged, and the inflow statistics pinned here call major inflows themselves barotropic. The replacement argues from the salinity difference between bed and surface alone.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-CC-C4-SECONDARY("An event should raise near-bed salinity more than surface ...")
  E-CC-MOHR-HALOCLINE[("Mohrholz (2018): the · halocline limits ventilation")]
  D-LR-REGISTER[("The hypothesis register · data/derived/hypotheses.json")]
  E-CC-MOHR-HALOCLINE --> C-CC-C4-SECONDARY
  D-LR-REGISTER --> C-CC-C4-SECONDARY
  style C-CC-C4-SECONDARY fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style E-CC-MOHR-HALOCLINE fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style D-LR-REGISTER fill:#1c4e70,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#e6edf3
```

- **external** — Mohrholz (2018): the halocline limits ventilation: “Strong stratification at the halocline limits vertical ventilation from the surface to the top mixed layer” ([`CC-MOHRHOLZ-2018`](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2018.00384/pdf), pinned). Strong stratification at the halocline limits vertical ventilation from the surface.
- **held** — The hypothesis register data/derived/hypotheses.json. The mechanisms HYPOTHESES.md lists, in their groups.

<a id="C-CC-C4-INDEX"></a>
### The event index: eastward wind at the southern point, from speed and direction, as a daily mean; its [10](SOURCES.md#F-eb88322a13)-day running sum is the westerly burst, multiplied by the easterly deficit of the [35](SOURCES.md#F-1e328e10eb) days before it, with a gap of [5](SOURCES.md#F-6270109e4e) days, as preconditioning; winter maxima give the event onsets.

`C-CC-C4-INDEX` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** Mohrholz (2018) describes wind and air-pressure differences as setting up the sea-level difference between the Kattegat and the western Baltic that drives barotropic inflows; the index encodes a westerly burst after an easterly spell. Its windows are stated design values, not fitted, and the southern point is the one of the three nearest the straits.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-CC-C4-INDEX("The event index: eastward wind at the southern point, from...")
  E-CC-MOHR-WIND[("Mohrholz (2018): wind · drives barotropic inflows")]
  C-CC-C4-WIND("The three Baltic wind files each hold hourly wind speed an...")
  H-CC-WIND[("Baltic wind files · data/raw/marine/wind_baltic_*.json")]
  X-CC-C4PAGE["hypodraft_c4.py"]
  E-CC-MOHR-WIND --> C-CC-C4-INDEX
  C-CC-C4-WIND --> C-CC-C4-INDEX
  H-CC-WIND --> C-CC-C4-WIND
  X-CC-C4PAGE --> C-CC-C4-WIND
  style C-CC-C4-INDEX fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style E-CC-MOHR-WIND fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style C-CC-C4-WIND fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style H-CC-WIND fill:#1c4e70,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#e6edf3
  style X-CC-C4PAGE fill:#21262d,stroke:#8b949e,color:#c9d1d9
```

- **external** — Mohrholz (2018): wind drives barotropic inflows: “Wind forcing and air pressure differences establish sea level differences between the Kattegat and the western Baltic, which drive barotropic inflow events” ([`CC-MOHRHOLZ-2018`](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2018.00384/pdf), pinned). Wind and air-pressure differences set up the sea-level difference between the Kattegat and the western Baltic that drives barotropic inflows.
- **claim** — The three Baltic wind files each hold hourly wind speed and direction at one point from 1995-01-01T00:00 to 2025-12-31T23:00 with no value missing; all three points lie east of Bornholm, so none is over the Kattegat or the Belts. ([`C-CC-C4-WIND`](CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-WIND))

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-CC-C4-NULLRULE"></a>
### The null is not the statistic's nominal one: deep water in the central Baltic is renewed by major inflows and otherwise stagnates, so a Gotland deep series persists from month to month and crosses a threshold set for independent months more often than it allows; the null is computed on surrogates that keep that persistence.

`C-CC-C4-NULLRULE` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** Mohrholz (2018) calls major inflows the only source of deep-water ventilation in the central Baltic basins and describes long stagnation periods between them, so a deep series changes in steps and stays put between; a persistent series crosses a threshold set for independent values more often than the threshold allows, and surrogates that keep the persistence give a threshold that does not.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C4-QUOTEDNULL): Neither the order of magnitude nor the effective sample size was computed or sourced. The case for a computed null stands without them.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-CC-C4-NULLRULE("The null is not the statistic's nominal one: deep water in...")
  E-CC-MOHR-SOLE[("Mohrholz (2018): inflows · are the only deep ventilation")]
  E-CC-MOHR-STAG[("Mohrholz (2018): long · stagnation between inflows")]
  E-CC-MOHR-SOLE --> C-CC-C4-NULLRULE
  E-CC-MOHR-STAG --> C-CC-C4-NULLRULE
  style C-CC-C4-NULLRULE fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style E-CC-MOHR-SOLE fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-CC-MOHR-STAG fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
```

- **external** — Mohrholz (2018): inflows are the only deep ventilation: “They are the solely source for deep water ventilation in the central Baltic basins” ([`CC-MOHRHOLZ-2018`](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2018.00384/pdf), pinned). Major inflows are the only source of deep-water ventilation in the central Baltic basins.
- **external** — Mohrholz (2018): long stagnation between inflows: “followed by long lasting stagnation periods in the central Baltic basins” ([`CC-MOHRHOLZ-2018`](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2018.00384/pdf), pinned). The inflow series show long stagnation periods in the central Baltic basins.

<a id="C-CC-C4-N1"></a>
### The primary null shifts the event index circularly by whole years, over the years from 1995, when the wind begins, that index and responses share; the smallest p it can give is one over the number of alignments, the true one included, and no result is stated beyond it.

`C-CC-C4-N1` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** A whole-year shift moves every event to the same season of another year, so seasonality, any seasonal pattern of sampling and each series' autocorrelation survive and only the pairing with the responses is broken; with the true alignment one among the alignments tried, no p can be smaller than one over their number.

<a id="C-CC-C4-PANELNULL"></a>
### The panel's stations are not replicates: neighbouring positions sampled in the same months can see the same water, so the statistic is the median across positions of a per-station z-anomaly, the panel shifts as one, the null is over time only, the sensitivity run is one fit per station reported as a distribution of lags, and a signal only the composite shows is the composite's.

`C-CC-C4-PANELNULL` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** Anomalies that share water are not independent, so treating stations as replicates would count one signal many times; shifting the panel as one keeps their dependence inside the null, and single-station fits show whether the composite's signal is in the stations.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C4-REPLICATES): The station count came from the panel made in a drafting session whose code and output are not held, and nothing here re-derives it, and nothing here shows that the positions form one hydrographic regime. The argument stands without either.

<a id="C-CC-C4-P5"></a>
### The statistic is Kendall τ of peak lag against the sites' order along the path; τ depends only on ranks, so the order gives the same statistic as any distances that keep it.

`C-CC-C4-P5` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** Kendall's τ counts the pairs of sites whose lags are ordered the same way as their positions, so it depends only on the order of the positions; distances along the path are in that order, so they would give the same τ.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C4-DIST): The distances have no source held or pinned here, and Kendall's τ does not need them: it depends only on the order of the sites along the path.

<a id="C-CC-C4-P7"></a>
### Secondary: the same on the bed-minus-surface salinity difference, and a check on oxy_bed for a rise followed by a fall, the pulse ventilating and then stratifying.

`C-CC-C4-P7` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** [C4](hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") has the pulses both ventilate and strengthen stratification, and the inflowing water is saline and oxygen-rich, as Mohrholz (2018) describes; at a station the first would raise bed oxygen and the second, by limiting mixing from above, could then lower it.

- **external** — Mohrholz (2018): inflowing water is oxygen-rich: “The inflowing saline and oxygen rich water reached the central Baltic OMZ and turned the former anoxic deep water to oxic conditions” ([`CC-MOHRHOLZ-2018`](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2018.00384/pdf), pinned). The inflowing water is saline and oxygen-rich, and turned anoxic deep water oxic.
- **external** — Mohrholz (2018): the halocline limits ventilation: “Strong stratification at the halocline limits vertical ventilation from the surface to the top mixed layer” ([`CC-MOHRHOLZ-2018`](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2018.00384/pdf), pinned). Strong stratification at the halocline limits vertical ventilation from the surface.

<a id="C-CC-C4-WOULD"></a>
### A broken order would be a clean falsification, cheap and robust to any error that shifts or rescales a series without moving when its peak falls, because τ uses only the order of the peak lags; otherwise the result is weak corroboration, capped at the primary null's p floor.

`C-CC-C4-WOULD` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** τ uses only the order of the peak lags, so an error that leaves each peak where it falls cannot move it; the smallest p the shift null can give caps any corroboration.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C4-EVENTS): The cap followed from a shift count the design cannot make; the event count and the single large event were asserted without the inflow record, which is not held; and the oxygen record runs to 2025-01.

<a id="C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE"></a>
### sal_bed, temp_bed and oxysat_bed come from the same CTD casts; salinity is estimated from conductivity and saturation is oxygen as a share of what water holds at its temperature and salinity, so they are one piece of evidence, not three.

`C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C4.md](hypodrafts/C4.md).

**Why it follows:** The monthly panel takes every variable from the same CTD casts; practical salinity is built on conductivity, and saturation expresses oxygen against a solubility set by temperature and salinity, so an error in one channel reaches the others.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE("sal_bed, temp_bed and oxysat_bed come from the same CTD ca...")
  X-CC-STSERIES["stations_series.py"]
  E-CC-WIKI-PSS[("Salinity: estimated from · electrical conductivity")]
  E-CC-WIKI-O2SAT[("Oxygen saturation: · a share of the maximum")]
  E-CC-USGS-FUNC[("USGS: solubility is a function · of temperature, salinity, pressure")]
  U-KP-PSS(("Trail ends: channel · definitions not pinned"))
  X-CC-STSERIES --> C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE
  E-CC-WIKI-PSS --> C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE
  E-CC-WIKI-O2SAT --> C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE
  E-CC-USGS-FUNC --> C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE
  U-KP-PSS --> C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE
  style C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style X-CC-STSERIES fill:#21262d,stroke:#8b949e,color:#c9d1d9
  style E-CC-WIKI-PSS fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-CC-WIKI-O2SAT fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-CC-USGS-FUNC fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style U-KP-PSS fill:#262626,stroke:#ff7b72,color:#e6edf3,stroke-dasharray:2 2
```

- **script** — stations_series.py. For each CTD cast, splits its depth range into quarters, keeps the shallowest as the surface and the deepest as the bed, and writes each variable's median per station and month, taken separately for each variable, to docs/data/areas/stations_series.bin.
- **external** — Salinity: estimated from electrical conductivity: “The use of electrical conductivity measurements to estimate the ionic content of seawater led to the development of the scale called the practical salinity scale” ([`CC-WIKI-SALINITY`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salinity), pinned). Practical salinity is a scale built on electrical conductivity measurements.
- **external** — Oxygen saturation: a share of the maximum: “as a proportion of the maximal concentration that can be dissolved in that medium at the given temperature” ([`CC-WIKI-O2SAT`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen_saturation), pinned). Saturation is oxygen as a proportion of the most the medium can dissolve at its temperature.
- **external** — USGS: solubility is a function of temperature, salinity, pressure: “All three terms are a function of water temperature. In addition, the salinity correction factor is a function of salinity and the pressure correction factor is a function of barometric pressure” ([`CC-USGS-OWQ-2011-03`](https://water.usgs.gov/water-resources/memos/documents/WQ.2011.03.pdf), pinned). Dissolved-oxygen solubility is a freshwater baseline times a salinity factor and a pressure factor, all functions of temperature, the salinity factor also of salinity and the pressure factor of pressure.
- **trail ends here** — Trail ends: channel definitions not pinned. That practical salinity is computed from conductivity and temperature, and oxygen saturation from oxygen, temperature and salinity, is the standard definition - the practical salinity scale and the oxygen solubility equations. No document stating it is pinned in this project (checked 2026-09-11).

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-CC-C6-CEILING"></a>
### Oxygen solubility is a function of temperature and salinity, and of pressure, computed from published equations, of which Weiss (1970) proposed the set the draft uses; that half of [C6](hypodrafts/C6.md "Water temperature and solubility") needs no test.

`C-CC-C6-CEILING` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C6.md](hypodrafts/C6.md).

**Why it follows:** The USGS memorandum writes dissolved-oxygen solubility as a freshwater baseline times a salinity factor and a pressure factor, all functions of temperature, and describes Weiss's equations as computing solubility from temperature and salinity; a fixed function of measured variables needs no test.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-CC-C6-CEILING("Oxygen solubility is a function of temperature and salinit...")
  E-CC-USGS-FUNC[("USGS: solubility is a function · of temperature, salinity, pressure")]
  E-CC-USGS-WEISS[("USGS: Weiss's equations")]
  E-CC-USGS-FUNC --> C-CC-C6-CEILING
  E-CC-USGS-WEISS --> C-CC-C6-CEILING
  style C-CC-C6-CEILING fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style E-CC-USGS-FUNC fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-CC-USGS-WEISS fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
```

- **external** — USGS: solubility is a function of temperature, salinity, pressure: “All three terms are a function of water temperature. In addition, the salinity correction factor is a function of salinity and the pressure correction factor is a function of barometric pressure” ([`CC-USGS-OWQ-2011-03`](https://water.usgs.gov/water-resources/memos/documents/WQ.2011.03.pdf), pinned). Dissolved-oxygen solubility is a freshwater baseline times a salinity factor and a pressure factor, all functions of temperature, the salinity factor also of salinity and the pressure factor of pressure.
- **external** — USGS: Weiss's equations: “Weiss proposed a set of equations to compute oxygen solubility in water as a function of water temperature and salinity” ([`CC-USGS-OWQ-2011-03`](https://water.usgs.gov/water-resources/memos/documents/WQ.2011.03.pdf), pinned). Weiss proposed equations for oxygen solubility as a function of water temperature and salinity.

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-CC-C6-NEUTRAL"></a>
### D is solubility-neutral by construction: if temperature acted on near-bed oxygen only through the ceiling, D would not depend on temperature.

`C-CC-C6-NEUTRAL` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C6.md](hypodrafts/C6.md).

**Why it follows:** D measures the distance below the ceiling at the water's own temperature and salinity; a temperature effect on the ceiling alone moves the ceiling, not the distance below it, which consumption and supply set.

- **the argument alone** — nothing further is cited: the reasoning above is the whole of it, for the reader to judge

<a id="C-CC-C6-SUBSID"></a>

`C-CC-C6-SUBSID` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

<a id="C-CC-C6-NOTOUTCOME"></a>
### The archive's oxysat_bed is never the outcome: saturation is oxygen as a share of what the water can hold at its temperature, so regressing it on temperature would put temperature on both sides.

`C-CC-C6-NOTOUTCOME` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C6.md](hypodrafts/C6.md).

**Why it follows:** Saturation is oxygen as a proportion of the most the water can dissolve at its temperature, and that solubility is a function of temperature, so temperature would stand on both sides of the regression.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C6-RECOMPUTE): How ODA computes its saturation is not documented in anything held or pinned here, and the recomputation was run in a drafting session whose code and output are not held.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-CC-C6-NOTOUTCOME("The archive's oxysat_bed is never the outcome: saturation ...")
  E-CC-WIKI-O2SAT[("Oxygen saturation: · a share of the maximum")]
  E-CC-USGS-FUNC[("USGS: solubility is a function · of temperature, salinity, pressure")]
  E-CC-WIKI-O2SAT --> C-CC-C6-NOTOUTCOME
  E-CC-USGS-FUNC --> C-CC-C6-NOTOUTCOME
  style C-CC-C6-NOTOUTCOME fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style E-CC-WIKI-O2SAT fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-CC-USGS-FUNC fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
```

- **external** — Oxygen saturation: a share of the maximum: “as a proportion of the maximal concentration that can be dissolved in that medium at the given temperature” ([`CC-WIKI-O2SAT`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen_saturation), pinned). Saturation is oxygen as a proportion of the most the medium can dissolve at its temperature.
- **external** — USGS: solubility is a function of temperature, salinity, pressure: “All three terms are a function of water temperature. In addition, the salinity correction factor is a function of salinity and the pressure correction factor is a function of barometric pressure” ([`CC-USGS-OWQ-2011-03`](https://water.usgs.gov/water-resources/memos/documents/WQ.2011.03.pdf), pinned). Dissolved-oxygen solubility is a freshwater baseline times a salinity factor and a pressure factor, all functions of temperature, the salinity factor also of salinity and the pressure factor of pressure.

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

*Confirmed 2026-09-11 by* `agent w3-cc (read each C6 sentence as recorded in claim_spans.json against its register entry, reasoning and what it rests on: hypodraft_facts.json, hypodraft_ctd.json and enums.json as printed, stations_series.py and hypodraft_ctd.py code, the pinned USGS 2011.03 and Wikipedia phrases, and the claims of other pages it rests on; 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)`. *If anything shown here changes, this claim is refused until it is read again.*

<a id="C-CC-C6-DELIBERATE"></a>
### D contains temperature through C_sat deliberately: that removes the solubility channel rather than making the test circular, because C_sat is a fixed published function, not fitted to these data.

`C-CC-C6-DELIBERATE` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C6.md](hypodrafts/C6.md).

**Why it follows:** C_sat is computed from temperature and salinity by equations published before these data were collected and not adjusted to them, so it carries no information from the deficit it is compared with.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C6-EXACT): The equations are not exact: the USGS memorandum pinned here records differences between Weiss's predictions and Benson and Krause's, and USGS replaced Weiss's. The replacement says what holds: a fixed published function, not fitted to these data.

<a id="C-CC-C6-EIV"></a>
### An error in temperature enters D through C_sat, which falls as temperature rises, and enters the regressor unchanged, so it pulls the slope toward a negative value as well as toward none; the test is conservative in the direction that matters. Salinity, derived from conductivity and temperature, carries temperature error too; the size of either effect has not been computed here.

`C-CC-C6-EIV` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/C6.md](hypodrafts/C6.md).

**Why it follows:** With the observed temperature the true one plus an error, the deficit picks up the error times the slope of solubility on temperature, which is negative because solubility falls as water warms, while the regressor picks it up unchanged; the covariance gains a negative term and the variance a positive one, so the estimated slope is pulled below the true one and toward none.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-CC-OLD-C6-EIV): The slopes, spreads and propagated errors were computed in a drafting session whose code is not held. The sign argument stands without them, and the magnitudes are left uncomputed.

```mermaid
  C-CC-C6-EIV("An error in temperature enters D through C_sat, which fall...")
  E-PC-DCE23-TEMP[("DCE oxygen note: · warm water promotes iltsvind")]
  E-OB-ML-SOLUB[("Middelburg and Levin: · warming lowers solubility")]
  E-CC-WIKI-PSS[("Salinity: estimated from · electrical conductivity")]
  U-KP-PSS(("Trail ends: channel · definitions not pinned"))
  U-CC-NORUN(("Trail ends: no script · runs either test"))
  E-PC-DCE23-TEMP --> C-CC-C6-EIV
  E-OB-ML-SOLUB --> C-CC-C6-EIV
  E-CC-WIKI-PSS --> C-CC-C6-EIV
  U-KP-PSS --> C-CC-C6-EIV
  U-CC-NORUN --> C-CC-C6-EIV
  style C-CC-C6-EIV fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style E-PC-DCE23-TEMP fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-OB-ML-SOLUB fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-CC-WIKI-PSS fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style U-KP-PSS fill:#262626,stroke:#ff7b72,color:#e6edf3,stroke-dasharray:2 2
  style U-CC-NORUN fill:#262626,stroke:#ff7b72,color:#e6edf3,stroke-dasharray:2 2
```

- **external** — DCE oxygen note:
warm water promotes iltsvind: “Høj vandtemperatur fremmer iltsvind” ([`NI-DCE-ILT-2023`](https://dce.au.dk/fileadmin/dce.au.dk/Udgivelser/Notater_2023/N2023_52.pdf), pinned). High water temperature promotes iltsvind, since oxygen consumption rises with temperature and oxygen's solubility falls.
- **external** — Middelburg and Levin: warming lowers solubility: “Global warming will lead to reduced oxygen solubility” ([`ML2009-HYPOXIA`](https://bg.copernicus.org/articles/6/1273/2009/bg-6-1273-2009.pdf), pinned)
- **external** — Salinity: estimated from electrical conductivity: “The use of electrical conductivity measurements to estimate the ionic content of seawater led to the development of the scale called the practical salinity scale” ([`CC-WIKI-SALINITY`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salinity), pinned). Practical salinity is a scale built on electrical conductivity measurements.
- **trail ends here** — Trail ends: channel definitions not pinned. That practical salinity is computed from conductivity and temperature, and oxygen saturation from oxygen, temperature and salinity, is the standard definition - the practical salinity scale and the oxygen solubility equations. No document stating it is pinned in this project (checked 2026-09-11).
- **trail ends here** — Trail ends: no script runs either test. Searched `scripts/*.py` and `scripts/pages/*.py` on 2026-09-11 for code computing a wind-driven inflow index, a superposed-epoch composite, a Kendall statistic across sites, an oxygen solubility (`C_sat`, Weiss, Benson and Krause), a join of the near-bed arrays or a within-cell slope of deficit on temperature. The inflow files are read only by `fetch_cmems.py`, which downloads them, and docs/data/baltic/gotland.json only by `landing_facts.py`, which counts months under the iltsvind threshold; `C_sat` appears only in the prose of other drafts. Member states provided the data to ICES, and its working group on spatial fisheries data processed them to c-square products at HELCOM's request.
- **external** — HELCOM record: by year and quarter, per c-square: “* quarter ### spatial resolution: * c-square” ([`DZ-HELCOM-META`](https://metadata.helcom.fi/geonetwork/srv/api/records/0195e2c6-6b83-49ea-a0db-41f14a316c87/formatters/xml), pinned). Each layer's temporal resolution is given as year and quarter, and its spatial resolution as the c-square.
- **external** — HELCOM record: intensity of mobile bottom-contacting gears: “Intensity of mobile bottom contacting gears” ([`DZ-HELCOM-META`](https://metadata.helcom.fi/geonetwork/srv/api/records/0195e2c6-6b83-49ea-a0db-41f14a316c87/formatters/xml), pinned)
- **external** — HELCOM record: the gear groups: “* Dredge (DRB) * Demersal seine (SDN, SSC) * Otter trawl” ([`DZ-HELCOM-META`](https://metadata.helcom.fi/geonetwork/srv/api/records/0195e2c6-6b83-49ea-a0db-41f14a316c87/formatters/xml), pinned). For the intensity layers the gear groups are the total, dredge, demersal seine and otter trawl, with Benthis metiers beside them.
- **external** — HELCOM record: swept area and swept-area ratio: “* Subsurface SAR * Total weight” ([`DZ-HELCOM-META`](https://metadata.helcom.fi/geonetwork/srv/api/records/0195e2c6-6b83-49ea-a0db-41f14a316c87/formatters/xml), pinned). The intensity layers give surface and subsurface swept area and swept-area ratio, with weight, value and fishing hours.
- **external** — HELCOM record: the shapefile field names: “sur_sar = surface_sar * subsur_sar = subsurface_sar” ([`DZ-HELCOM-META`](https://metadata.helcom.fi/geonetwork/srv/api/records/0195e2c6-6b83-49ea-a0db-41f14a316c87/formatters/xml), pinned). Shapefile field names are cut to ten characters, so surface and subsurface SAR appear as sur_sar and subsur_sar.
- **external** — HELCOM record: SAR is never withheld for anonymity: “surface and subsurface SAR are not subject to anonymity constraints” ([`DZ-HELCOM-META`](https://metadata.helcom.fi/geonetwork/srv/api/records/0195e2c6-6b83-49ea-a0db-41f14a316c87/formatters/xml), pinned). Weight, value and fishing hours are withheld where too few vessels fished a cell; swept area and swept-area ratio are not.

<a id="C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY"></a>
### Neither null is a plain shuffle: effort and bathymetry are spatially autocorrelated, and on this project's nearest-neighbour station graph random connected partitions of matched sizes already agree with each other at the counted mean adjusted Rand index, an index corrected for chance against arbitrary partitions and not contiguous ones; a cell-wise shuffle of effort would repeat that mistake.

`C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/D1.md](hypodrafts/D1.md).

**Why it follows:** partition_contiguous.py measures the agreement contiguity alone buys on the stations' graph; a shuffle that ignores contiguity would credit that agreement to effort.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY("Neither null is a plain shuffle: effort and bathymetry are...")
  D-DZ-CONTIG[("Contiguous partitions · docs/data/areas/partition_contiguous.json")]
  X-DZ-CONTIG["partition_contiguous.py"]
  D-DZ-CONTIG --> C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY
  X-DZ-CONTIG --> C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY
  style C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style D-DZ-CONTIG fill:#1c4e70,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#e6edf3
  style X-DZ-CONTIG fill:#21262d,stroke:#8b949e,color:#c9d1d9
```

- **held** — Contiguous partitions docs/data/areas/partition_contiguous.json. Per station graph: how many stations it holds and the mean adjusted Rand index between random connected partitions of matched sizes, the floor any derived partition must beat. Its own note says a raw index is not readable here, because contiguity alone makes partitions agree above chance.
- **script** — partition_contiguous.py. contiguous_null grows random connected partitions by breadth-first accretion from random seeds, with group sizes matched to the official water bodies; main averages the adjusted Rand index over every pair of them for each graph and writes partition_contiguous.json.

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-DZ-D1-CONFOUND"></a>
### Trawlers fish where fish are, and fish are where productivity is, so a raw effort-oxygen association is that association read backwards; the within-station fixed effect, fluorescence and the substrate interaction break it only together.

`C-DZ-D1-CONFOUND` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/D1.md](hypodrafts/D1.md).

**Why it follows:** The fixed effect removes what is constant about a place; fluorescence absorbs the time-varying part of productivity; productivity-driven effort would lower oxygen wherever trawlers work, while resuspension can only do it where reduced fines exist.

- **the argument alone** — nothing further is cited: the reasoning above is the whole of it, for the reader to judge

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-KD-D7-WAVESHARE"></a>
### The wave model held here puts the modelled bed shear at its shallowest depth above the dead-bed threshold in most hours, so a monthly median describes a mixture, not an event.

`C-KD-D7-WAVESHARE` · **modelled** — the output of somebody's model of the world, not an observation of it

Said on [hypodrafts/D7.md](hypodrafts/D7.md).

**Why it follows:** waves.py gives the share of all hours in which the modelled shear at each depth exceeds the dead-bed critical stress; at the shallowest depth it is the share printed. A month then holds exceeding and non-exceeding hours together.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-KD-OLD-D7-STORM): The storm duration had no source. The share is now read from waves.json as the page is built.

<a id="C-KD-D7-MECH"></a>
### Under [D7](hypodrafts/D7.md "Storm-driven resuspension"), resuspension is depth-limited, substrate-limited and relaxes as fine sediment settles; the test reads these as restrictions per station-visit, net of station mean, month-of-year and year.

`C-KD-D7-MECH` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/D7.md](hypodrafts/D7.md).

**Why it follows:** The depth limit is the one waves.py computes, the orbital velocity at the bed falling with depth through sinh of wavenumber times depth; the substrate limit and the relaxation are the hypothesis's mechanism, taken as given for the test and not measured here.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-KD-D7-MECH("Under D7, resuspension is depth-limited, substrate-limited...")
  X-KD-WAVES["waves.py"]

  style C-KD-D7-MECH fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style X-KD-WAVES fill:#21262d,stroke:#8b949e,color:#c9d1d9
```

- **script** — waves.py. Wind to fetch-limited waves, orbital velocity and bed shear at fixed depths for Køge Bugt, hourly. fetch_lookup reads the fetch from data/raw/weather/fetch.json, which seabed.py also reads and no script in the repository writes; bed_shear computes the orbital velocity through sinh of wavenumber times depth.

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-KD-D7-P-DEPTH"></a>
### Depth: clarity is degraded in the stated days after an hour of critical-shear exceedance at a station, scaling with the depth attenuation term, large in the shallow arm and zero within noise in the deep control, in the same storms.

`C-KD-D7-P-DEPTH` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/D7.md](hypodrafts/D7.md).

**Why it follows:** Deep beds feel little orbital velocity from the same wind, so a storm that clouds shallow stations and not deep ones is resuspension rather than weather; the window and the arms are stated values.

<a id="C-KD-D7-P-RELAX"></a>
### Relaxation: the coefficient decays monotonically over the stated days after an exceedance; a step persisting for weeks is a season, not a storm.

`C-KD-D7-P-RELAX` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/D7.md](hypodrafts/D7.md).

**Why it follows:** Settling returns the water to its prior clarity, so a storm's effect should fade with time since it; a persistent step has a slower cause.

`C-KD-D7-FALSIFY` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

- **script** — seabed.py. Computes from wind alone: wave-driven bed shear stress, how much more often a dead bed resuspends than a live one, and how often wind drives surface material onto the shore.

<a id="C-AF-F3-CIRC"></a>
### The eelgrass depth limit is, in DCE's words, an indicator of eutrophication and of the bottom-vegetation quality element, light attenuation is the factor that matters most for it, and the national models express it through Kd; regressing it on attenuation re-reads the relation the indicator is built on, not [F3](hypodrafts/F3.md "Loss of eelgrass and macroalgae").

`C-AF-F3-CIRC` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/F3.md](hypodrafts/F3.md).

**Why it follows:** DCE's report and DHI's model report say so in the phrases pinned. A regression of a quantity on the variable it is expressed through recovers the expression, whatever the feedback does.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-AF-F3-CIRC("The eelgrass depth limit is, in DCE's words, an indicator ...")
  E-AF-DCE-DEPTHLIM[("DCE: the eelgrass depth · limit as an indicator")]
  E-AF-DCE-KDFACTOR[("DCE: light attenuation · governs the depth limit")]
  E-AF-DHI-KD[("DHI and DCE models: · the depth limit through Kd")]
  E-AF-DCE-DEPTHLIM --> C-AF-F3-CIRC
  E-AF-DCE-KDFACTOR --> C-AF-F3-CIRC
  E-AF-DHI-KD --> C-AF-F3-CIRC
  style C-AF-F3-CIRC fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style E-AF-DCE-DEPTHLIM fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-AF-DCE-KDFACTOR fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
  style E-AF-DHI-KD fill:#3d3357,stroke:#a58cf0,color:#e6edf3
```

- **external** — DCE: the eelgrass depth limit as an indicator: “Ålegræssets dybdegrænse er en vigtig indikator for eutrofiering” ([`DCE-STATMOD-2015`](https://dce.au.dk/fileadmin/dce.au.dk/Udgivelser/Notater_2015/Dokumentation_statistiske_modeller_metoder_del3_28042015.pdf), pinned). DCE's report calls the eelgrass depth limit an important indicator of eutrophication and an indicator of the Water Framework Directive's bottom-vegetation quality element.
- **external** — DCE: light attenuation governs the depth limit: “den mest betydende faktor for ålegræssets dybdegrænse” ([`DCE-STATMOD-2015`](https://dce.au.dk/fileadmin/dce.au.dk/Udgivelser/Notater_2015/Dokumentation_statistiske_modeller_metoder_del3_28042015.pdf), pinned). The same report calls light attenuation the factor that matters most for the eelgrass depth limit.
- **external** — DHI and DCE models: the depth limit through Kd: “Bundvegetation: Ålegræssets dybdegrænse udtrykt ved Kd” ([`DHI-MODEL-DEL2-2015`](https://edit.mst.dk/media/lspfqzss/312-modeller-for-danske-fjorde-og-kystnaere-havomraader-del-2.pdf), pinned). The national mechanistic models describe the bottom-vegetation quality element as the eelgrass depth limit expressed through Kd.

<a id="C-GI-G1-ROUTES"></a>
### Warming reaches near-bed oxygen by the routes [G1](hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming") names - solubility, stratification and the rate of respiration - and only the first lowers near-bed oxygen whatever is consumed there; the other two act through the consumption beneath the stratified layer, which the load feeds.

`C-GI-G1-ROUTES` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** DCE's oxygen note states that oxygen's solubility in water falls with temperature and that the rate of oxygen consumption rises with it, and that eutrophication raises the production that sinks and is broken down at the bed, with depletion especially where the water column is stratified. Solubility sets the ceiling whatever is consumed; a faster respiration or a longer-isolated bottom layer lowers oxygen only through what there is to consume, which the load supplies.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-G1-SPLIT): The seasonal decomposition's figures were counted in a drafting session whose output and code are not held; Weiss (1970) was cited without being read or pinned here; and the metabolic route was called unmeasured without a search being recorded. The routes and the question are kept, argued from a pinned DCE note; the figures are dropped.

- **external** — DCE oxygen note:
warm water promotes iltsvind: “Høj vandtemperatur fremmer iltsvind” ([`NI-DCE-ILT-2023`](https://dce.au.dk/fileadmin/dce.au.dk/Udgivelser/Notater_2023/N2023_52.pdf), pinned). High water temperature promotes iltsvind, since oxygen consumption rises with temperature and oxygen's solubility falls.
- **external** — DCE oxygen note: eutrophication and the stratified bed: “Eutrofiering fører til øget produktion af planteplankton” ([`NI-DCE-ILT-2023`](https://dce.au.dk/fileadmin/dce.au.dk/Udgivelser/Notater_2023/N2023_52.pdf), pinned). Eutrophication raises the production of phytoplankton, which sinks and is broken down; oxygen consumption rises, and depletion can develop at the bed, especially where the water column is stratified.

<a id="C-GI-G1-CSAT"></a>
### Per station-month, C_sat is the oxygen solubility at the panel's near-bed temperature and salinity from a published solubility equation for seawater, in mg/l; then O_bed = C_sat(T_bed, S_bed) - D, so dO/dt = dC_sat/dt - dD/dt.

`C-GI-G1-CSAT` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** Taking the solubility from a published equation at the observed temperature and salinity makes the first term a computation on held values; the identity then defines the deficit as the remainder.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-G1-CSAT): Weiss (1970) was cited, and its conversion constant printed, without the paper being read or pinned here; and a solubility equation is an empirical fit, so calling it exact claimed more than can be shown.

- **the argument alone** — nothing further is cited: the reasoning above is the whole of it, for the reader to judge

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

*Confirmed 2026-09-11 by* `agent w3-gi (read each G1 and I1 sentence as the build recorded it against its claim, reasoning and what it rests on: the panel counts in drafts_b_counts.json, the station-register counts in hypotheses_evidence.json and hypodraft_facts.json, the CTD temperature decimals in hypodraft_ctd.json counted on OriginalResultat, stations_series.py's layer cut and median, flags.json as the panel's per-value flags, the pinned DCE 2023 oxygen note, and a search of scripts/ and data/derived/ for the computations and the station split; each retired passage as read out of git at 00a157f against its reason and replacement; 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)`. *If anything shown here changes, this claim is refused until it is read again.*

<a id="C-GI-G1-DEFICIT"></a>
### C_sat is computed from temperature and salinity by an equation from outside the archive, so the first term is computed, not estimated from it; the deficit D is solubility-neutral by construction and carries the rest: consumption, failed ventilation, advection.

`C-GI-G1-DEFICIT` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** The solubility equation is a fit made outside this archive, so none of its parameters is estimated from the data tested. D is what is left once the ceiling is subtracted, so whatever holds oxygen below the ceiling moves it, and the ceiling itself does not.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-G1-CSAT): Weiss (1970) was cited, and its conversion constant printed, without the paper being read or pinned here; and a solubility equation is an empirical fit, so calling it exact claimed more than can be shown.

<a id="C-GI-G1-BEDDEF"></a>
### Near the bed and near the surface are not fixed depths: stations_series.py takes, for each cast, the values in the deepest and in the shallowest part of the cast's own sampled depth range, cut at a fixed fraction of that range, and puts every such value in a station-month into one median, so D can pair temperature, salinity and oxygen from different casts and depths.

`C-GI-G1-BEDDEF` · **code** — what this project's code does, read from the code

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** stations_series.py computes, per cast, two cut depths a fixed fraction of the sampled range in from the shallowest and the deepest depth, appends each value beyond them to a list for its station, month and variable, and stores the median of each list; each variable has its own list.

```mermaid
  style D-KP-SERIES fill:#1c4e70,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#e6edf3
```

- **script** — stations_series.py. Streams the CTD extract cast by cast. Per cast it puts the values in the deepest and the shallowest part of the cast's sampled depth range, cut a fixed fraction in from each end, into lists per station, month and variable; it stores each list's median - the middle value, or the mean of the middle pair - as a point of a `uint16` station index, a `uint16` month index and a `float32` value, per variable at an offset in stations_series.bin.
- **held** — Monthly station series docs/data/areas/stations_series.json. One value per station and month for each variable, at the surface and at the bed (fluorescence at the surface only), written from the CTD extract; no instrument field.

<a id="C-GI-G1-CLOCK"></a>
### The CTD extract the panel is built from has no time of day in any row and no column for it; if the sampling hour drifted over the record, the diel oxygen cycle drifted with it, and nothing inside the panel can correct it, which caps the test rather than bounds it. The water-chemistry extract does carry clock values, which can bound the hour only where a cast shares its day with a bottle.

`C-GI-G1-CLOCK` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** The panel is written from the CTD extract, which carries a date and no clock (`C-HY-I3-NOCLOCK`); a diel cycle sampled at a drifting hour moves the monthly median with the hour, and no column in the panel records it. A clock borrowed from a same-day water-chemistry sample is the only way to place a cast in the day (`C-HY-I3-CHEMCLOCK`).

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-G1-ERRORS): The value ranges, the removed rows, the rounding figures and the count of cells without saturation come from a session whose output is not held. Most temperature rows of the CTD extract are written with more than one decimal, so it is not a one-decimal series. And the claim of no time-of-day column anywhere is wrong: the water-chemistry extract carries clock values.

<a id="C-GI-G1-CIRC"></a>
### Archived near-bed saturation is computed from oxygen, temperature and salinity, so it already contains temperature and is never an outcome here; D contains temperature through C_sat deliberately, the subtraction of the solubility channel with the equation coming from outside the archive, and errors in temperature enter D but not the year regressor, so they add noise, not trend.

`C-GI-G1-CIRC` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** Oxygen saturation is oxygen over its solubility at the sample's temperature and salinity, so a trend in it carries a trend in temperature. D subtracts the solubility on purpose, and an error in temperature that does not trend with the year cannot put a trend into D.

```mermaid
  style U-KP-PSS fill:#262626,stroke:#ff7b72,color:#e6edf3,stroke-dasharray:2 2
```

<a id="C-GI-G1-NULLDESIGN"></a>
### The null is not a zero slope but a year-block procedure under the constraint within station and within calendar month: resample the calendar years with replacement, and separately permute year labels attached to whole years, refitting on each draw; that keeps every station effect, the seasonal cycle and the within-year common shock, and destroys only the ordering of years against outcome.

`C-GI-G1-NULLDESIGN` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** Every cell in a year samples the same weather, so the year is the unit that can be exchanged; resampling station-months within years would treat a shared shock as independent draws.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-G1-NULL): The autocorrelations, the variance inflation and the standard errors were measured in a drafting session whose output and code are not held, and no script here computes them. The design of the null is kept without the figures.

- **the argument alone** — nothing further is cited: the reasoning above is the whole of it, for the reader to judge

<a id="C-GI-G1-DEFENCES"></a>
### If the mix of stations moves, it can tilt a pooled slope; the defences required are within-cell fixed effects, so a station only competes with itself, and the balanced panel, so entry and exit cannot tilt the slope.

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** A fixed effect per cell removes each station's level, so a station entering or leaving changes which cells are fitted, not the level a slope is measured against; a balanced panel keeps the same cells at both ends.

<a id="C-GI-G1-WOULDNOT"></a>
### It would not measure respiration, since D is a standing stock and converting to a rate needs a ventilation timescale the archive does not hold; a narrowing D fits load reduction working and a network drifting toward better-ventilated positions alike; and it says nothing about stratification beyond the difference between the ends of the sampled range, nothing about water bodies, nothing about the stations the span filter drops, and refutes `G1-b` only at the resolution of monthly medians taken at an unrecorded hour.

`C-GI-G1-WOULDNOT` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/G1.md](hypodrafts/G1.md).

**Why it follows:** D is an amount and a respiration rate is per unit time, and converting needs how fast the bottom water is renewed, which the panel does not hold. The defences bound drift in the network but cannot rule out a network that moved to better-ventilated positions. Near-bed and near-surface values are the ends of each cast's sampled range, not a measured pycnocline (`C-GI-G1-BEDDEF`); the panel holds monthly medians with no clock (`C-GI-G1-CLOCK`) and no water body (H-GI-SERIESMETA).

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-G1-WOULDNOT): It named the stations the span filter drops by a count no script here computes.

- **claim** — Near the bed and near the surface are not fixed depths: stations_series.py takes, for each cast, the values in the deepest and in the shallowest part of the cast's own sampled depth range, cut at a fixed fraction of that range, and puts every such value in a station-month into one median, so D can pair temperature, salinity and oxygen from different casts and depths. ([`C-GI-G1-BEDDEF`](CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-BEDDEF))
- **claim** — The CTD extract the panel is built from has no time of day in any row and no column for it; if the sampling hour drifted over the record, the diel oxygen cycle drifted with it, and nothing inside the panel can correct it, which caps the test rather than bounds it. The water-chemistry extract does carry clock values, which can bound the hour only where a cast shares its day with a bottle. ([`C-GI-G1-CLOCK`](CLAIMS.md#C-GI-G1-CLOCK))
- **held** — The panel's own header docs/data/areas/stations_series.json. Gives the first year, the monthly slots, the station list, each variable's count and byte offset, the layout of indices and values in stations_series.bin, and a note that which water body a station falls in is deliberately absent, as a model assumption kept in its own overlay.

<a id="C-GI-I1-CLOCK"></a>
### The CTD extract the panel is built from has no time of day in any row and no column for it, so the diel oxygen swing aliases into whichever hour the boat went, per station; the water-chemistry extract does carry clock values, which can bound the hour only where a cast shares its day with a bottle.

`C-GI-I1-CLOCK` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/I1.md](hypodrafts/I1.md).

**Why it follows:** The panel is written from the CTD extract, which carries a date and no clock (`C-HY-I3-NOCLOCK`); oxygen swings over the day, so a value from an unrecorded hour carries the swing. A clock borrowed from a same-day water-chemistry sample is the only way to place a cast in the day (`C-HY-I3-CHEMCLOCK`).

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-I1-CLASSES): The shares on each grid and the raw resolution of oxygen come from a session whose output is not held; and a time-of-day column does exist in the record, in the water-chemistry extract.

### The station is the resampling unit because observations are not independent within it; resampling observations would understate the band, by up to a factor of the square root of the observations per station when a station's observations move together.

`C-GI-I1-UNIT` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/I1.md](hypodrafts/I1.md).

**Why it follows:** The design effect of clustered sampling: the variance of a mean grows with the correlation within a station, up to the number of observations per station when they move together, so the standard error grows up to the square root of that number.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-I1-NULL): The panel's size and its number of stations were printed as counts from a session whose output is not held; the replicates and the band are design choices, now stated as such.

<a id="C-GI-I1-P1"></a>
### Read the binary at the near-bed oxygen offset the header gives; decode the station index, the month index and the value; the year is the first year plus the month index divided by twelve, rounded down, and the calendar month the remainder plus one.

`C-GI-I1-P1` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/I1.md](hypodrafts/I1.md).

**Why it follows:** The panel's header gives each variable's offset, the layout of indices and values and the first year; stations_series.py counts the month index in months since January of the first year.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-GI-OLD-I1-PROC): The run time, the memory, the panel's size and the counts of work were printed from a session whose output is not held.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-GI-I1-P1("Read the binary at the near-bed oxygen offset the header g...")
  H-GI-SERIESMETA[("The panel's own header · docs/data/areas/stations_series.json")]
  X-GI-SERIES["stations_series.py"]
  H-GI-SERIESMETA --> C-GI-I1-P1
  X-GI-SERIES --> C-GI-I1-P1
  style C-GI-I1-P1 fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
```

- **held** — The panel's own header docs/data/areas/stations_series.json. Gives the first year, the monthly slots, the station list, each variable's count and byte offset, the layout of indices and values in stations_series.bin, and a note that which water body a station falls in is deliberately absent, as a model assumption kept in its own overlay.
- **script** — stations_series.py. Streams the CTD extract cast by cast. Per cast it puts the values in the deepest and the shallowest part of the cast's sampled depth range, cut a fixed fraction in from each end, into lists per station, month and variable; it stores each list's median - the middle value, or the mean of the middle pair - as a point of a `uint16` station index, a `uint16` month index and a `float32` value, per variable at an offset in stations_series.bin.

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-IL-I3-A"></a>
### An extremal indicator, an annual minimum or a worst-month value, is an order statistic of the draws, so its expectation moves with the number of draws and with the months they fall in.

`C-IL-I3-A` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/I3.md](hypodrafts/I3.md).

**Why it follows:** The minimum of more draws from the same distribution is on average no larger, and the minimum of draws from months with lower values is lower; a worst-month value is formed the same way, from the extreme of the draws.

- **the argument alone** — nothing further is cited: the reasoning above is the whole of it, for the reader to judge

- **held** — Monthly station series docs/data/areas/stations_series.json. One value per station and month for each variable, at the surface and at the bed (fluorescence at the surface only), written from the CTD extract; no instrument field.
- **script** — stations_series.py. Streams the CTD extract one cast at a time. Writes docs/data/areas/stations_series.bin and stations_series.json, one station index, month index and value per station-month.

<a id="C-IL-I3-B-SUN"></a>
### Daylight at the stated latitude runs from its December to its June solstice length, so if oxygen follows the sun, sampling held to working hours meets a different phase of its daily cycle as the season moves; water-chemistry samples with an observed clock time rarely visit night or twilight.

`C-IL-I3-B-SUN` · **measured** — rests on measurement

Said on [hypodrafts/I3.md](hypodrafts/I3.md).

**Why it follows:** The day lengths are computed by hypotheses.py with daylight.py at a stated latitude; the same clock hour gives very different sun elevations at the two solstices; and the samples with an observed clock time leave night and twilight almost unvisited, both over the whole record and since the clock became a wall clock.

<a id="C-IL-I3-CLOCK"></a>
### The CTD extract behind the panel carries a date and no hour, as do the Secchi and light-attenuation extracts; the water-chemistry extract carries a clock value per sample, and depth_clock.py lends an observed bottle time to a CTD cast on the same station-day, assuming unchecked that the two share a moment.

`C-IL-I3-CLOCK` · **measured** — rests on measurement

Said on [hypodrafts/I3.md](hypodrafts/I3.md).

**Why it follows:** The extracts' headers carry no clock field except in water chemistry, where every genuine row has one; depth_clock.py lends only a clock that clock.py classes as an observed time, and whether cast and bottle share a moment is an unchecked assumption.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-IL-OLD-I3-NOCLOCK): Not true of the archive: the water-chemistry extract carries a clock value per sample, and a CTD cast sharing a station-day with a bottle whose clock is an observed time can borrow it, so the daily phase can be bounded there. <a id="C-IL-I3-B"></a>
### The daily phase cannot be scored on the panel, whose values carry no hour; it could be bounded only through borrowed clocks, which this page does not use, and nothing in the archive constrains the pre-dawn minimum; nothing here licenses a claim that the daily-cycle confound is absent or small.

<a id="C-IL-I3-TEST"></a>
### If the count-and-window half is right, an extremal indicator under fixed effort and a fixed calendar window follows a different path through the years than the same indicator on whatever visits each station-year contains; if the two coincide inside the resampling envelope, it is refuted as an explanation of the [O1](HYPOTHESES.md "Oxygen deficit") trend.

`C-IL-I3-TEST` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/I3.md](hypodrafts/I3.md).

**Why it follows:** The test this page sets: holding effort and window fixed removes exactly what the hypothesis says drives the indicator, so a difference between the two paths is its signature and agreement refutes it.

<a id="C-IL-I3-TWO"></a>
### The count and the window must be separated, because they can push opposite ways.

`C-IL-I3-TWO` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/I3.md](hypodrafts/I3.md).

**Why it follows:** More draws lower the expected minimum, while a sparse programme placed in the months when oxygen is lowest finds low values with few draws; the two effects can therefore offset each other in an indicator that mixes them.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-IL-OLD-I3-CANCEL): That the two effects nearly cancel came from a one-off run in the drafting session whose code and output are not held.

- **the argument alone** — nothing further is cited: the reasoning above is the whole of it, for the reader to judge

<a id="C-IL-I3-COUNT"></a>
### More draws, lower minimum, mechanically.

`C-IL-I3-COUNT` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/I3.md](hypodrafts/I3.md).

**Why it follows:** The minimum over a set of draws cannot rise when a draw is added, so its expectation falls with the number of draws whatever the water does.

<a id="C-IL-I3-WINDOW"></a>
### Which months the draws fall in matters as well as how many; how the panel's sparsely sampled station-years spread over the calendar has not been counted here.

`C-IL-I3-WINDOW` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/I3.md](hypodrafts/I3.md).

- **held** — Monthly station series docs/data/areas/stations_series.json. One value per station and month for each variable, at the surface and at the bed (fluorescence at the surface only), written from the CTD extract; no instrument field.
- **script** — stations_series.py. Streams the CTD extract one cast at a time. Within a cast, values in the shallowest quarter of its depth range go to the surface and values in the deepest quarter to the bed; the panel value is the median of every parseable value per station, month and variable, with no test of range. Writes docs/data/areas/stations_series.bin and stations_series.json, one station index, month index and value per station-month.
- **script** — cube.py. Fixes the monthly grid the station series indexes its months by: from January of the constant `Y0` to December of `Y1`, both set in the script. mon() gives a date outside those years no month index, and stations_series.py skips such a cast.
- **script** — drafts_b_counts.py. Counts, from the files themselves, the monthly panel's variables, the Secchi extract's records and easting columns, the seabed layer's classes and the CMEMS plankton files, their years and variables; writes data/derived/drafts_b_counts.json.
- **held** — Held-file counts data/derived/drafts_b_counts.json. What drafts_b_counts.py counted, including the panel's variables, the Secchi extract's records and repeated easting column, the seabed classes and the plankton files with their first, last and partial years.
- **script** — hypodraft_facts.py. File facts for the drafts: the wind record, the area partition, the probe enumeration and the flagged sign flips.
- **held** — Draft file facts data/derived/hypodraft_facts.json. Written by hypodraft_facts.py: among other facts, the first year of the monthly station series, and the station-months and stations the flag record marks as a batch sign flip.

<a id="C-KD-K1-DERIVED"></a>
### Each functional-type field is, by the provider's own note in the files, derived from chlorophyll, so it cannot move where chlorophyll does not; [K1](hypodrafts/K1.md "Silicon depletion and the diatom-to-flagellate shift")'s distinguishing prediction, that composition moves while total biomass need not, cannot be expressed in these files, let alone tested.

`C-KD-K1-DERIVED` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/K1.md](hypodrafts/K1.md).

**Why it follows:** Premises: the variable attributes in the files say each type is derived from chlorophyll as in Brando et al. (2021), and the product description says the types are evaluated by a region-specific algorithm. If each type is computed from the chlorophyll of the same cell and day, then at fixed chlorophyll every type is fixed, and a change in composition without a change in chlorophyll cannot be represented. The argument is void if the algorithm uses anything beyond chlorophyll (A-KD-FUNCTION).

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-KD-OLD-K1-REACH): The counts from external endpoints were made in a drafting session whose output and code are not held, so they cannot be checked; that the counts are openly reachable is not established, and none is held. The page now says what is held and what is not, and the chlorophyll point rests on the files' own description.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-KD-OLD-K1-PARTITION): Computed in a one-off run whose output and code are not held. The files' own description, that each type is derived from chlorophyll, supports the conclusion without those figures.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-KD-OLD-K1-RELABEL): 'Monotone' and 'measure zero' rested on the unheld run above. What the held files support is narrower: each type is, by their own note, derived from chlorophyll, so it cannot move where chlorophyll does not.

<a id="C-KD-K1-TEST"></a>
### The test: at a sampling position, regress the March-April diatom share of phytoplankton carbon on the preceding January-February median surface Si:DIN, with position fixed effects; [K1](hypodrafts/K1.md "Silicon depletion and the diatom-to-flagellate shift") predicts a positive slope that survives conditioning on total chlorophyll.

`C-KD-K1-TEST` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/K1.md](hypodrafts/K1.md).

**Why it follows:** Working at a sampling position keeps the test off any partition into water bodies, which would be an assumption laid over the stations; the pre-bloom pool comes before the bloom it is said to shape; conditioning on chlorophyll separates composition from biomass, which is the hypothesis's distinguishing prediction.

<a id="C-KD-K1-FIXED"></a>
### Hence position fixed effects and a balanced panel; a station-level permutation is not conservative enough.

`C-KD-K1-FIXED` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/K1.md](hypodrafts/K1.md).

**Why it follows:** Fixed effects compare a position with itself, so a changing mix of positions cannot move the slope, and a balanced panel keeps the mix fixed. Neighbouring stations can share water, so their residuals need not be independent, and a permutation across stations treats them as if they were.

- **held** — Monthly station series docs/data/areas/stations_series.json. One value per station and month for each variable, at the surface and at the bed (fluorescence at the surface only), written from the CTD extract; no instrument field.
- **script** — stations_series.py. Streams the CTD extract one cast at a time. Within a cast, values in the shallowest quarter of its depth range go to the surface and values in the deepest quarter to the bed; the panel value is the median of every parseable value per station, month and variable, with no test of range. Writes docs/data/areas/stations_series.bin and stations_series.json, one station index, month index and value per station-month.
- **script** — cube.py. Fixes the monthly grid the station series indexes its months by: from January of the constant `Y0` to December of `Y1`, both set in the script. mon() gives a date outside those years no month index, and stations_series.py skips such a cast.
- **script** — drafts_b_counts.py. Counts, from the files themselves, the monthly panel's variables, the Secchi extract's records and easting columns, the seabed layer's classes and the CMEMS plankton files, their years and variables; writes data/derived/drafts_b_counts.json.
- **held** — Held-file counts data/derived/drafts_b_counts.json. What drafts_b_counts.py counted, including the panel's variables, the Secchi extract's records and repeated easting column, the seabed classes and the plankton files with their first, last and partial years.
- **script** — hypodraft_facts.py. File facts for the drafts: the wind record, the area partition, the probe enumeration and the flagged sign flips.
- **held** — Draft file facts data/derived/hypodraft_facts.json. Written by hypodraft_facts.py: among other facts, the first year of the monthly station series, and the station-months and stations the flag record marks as a batch sign flip.

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.

<a id="C-IL-L3-H0"></a>
### With no trend at all each window's slope is noise, as likely positive as negative, so both signs across the windows are expected and a sign flip on its own does not tell a trend from none.

`C-IL-L3-H0` · **argued** — follows by reasoning from what it rests on - the argument is given in full

Said on [hypodrafts/L3.md](hypodrafts/L3.md).

**Why it follows:** Under a symmetric noise model with zero mean slope, a fitted slope's sign is a coin toss, so windows disagreeing in sign is what no trend produces; a sign flip cannot therefore be evidence against a trend or for one.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-IL-OLD-L3-H0): The share and the median range came from the unheld simulation.

`C-TR-RULE` · **provisional** — unchecked - see the graph for what would check it

Said on [hypodrafts/TRIAGE.md](hypodrafts/TRIAGE.md).

**Why it follows:** The rows were written against the register's entry for each hypothesis, the held extracts and layers counted in data/derived, the page's own count of section stations, and rescore.json; the numbers in a blocker are live figures, and an absence is phrased as not found. The classes are judgements on those blockers, so the rule licenses a blocker as a record of what was found and the class as one reading of it.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-TR-OLD-TABLE): Its classes for the hypotheses that waited on the water-chemistry extract predate the fetch; rows carried numbers only as quotations of this page's earlier version; blockers were contradicted by the source register or the held files - an extract holding total alkalinity said to hold one carbonate variable, replicate grabs said not to exist, open sequencing and a sediment core record said to exist or not to exist against what the register found - and some cited other pages for what those pages no longer say. The table is rebuilt row by row from the register, the held files and the re-score, and the classes follow.

- **held** — Source register data/manual/data_sources*.json. This project's catalogue of data sources: what each holds, how it is produced - measured, modelled or retrieved from satellite - and when it was checked.
- **held** — The sources surveyed data/manual/data_sources*.json. Every source this project looked at for each hypothesis, with what it holds and what it lacks. The triage's 'unscoreable' means the deciding measurement is in none of these.

Carries a clock value on every genuine row, though for much of the old record the value is a filled-in default rather than a time (scripts/clockzone.py); several parameters appear under more than one unit - see DATA_SOURCES.md.
- **held** — ODA CTD [53,710,760](SOURCES.md#F-4df017f985) rows. Oxygen, temperature, salinity at depth. NO clock field: ODA offers none for this topic.
- **held** — rescore.json. data/derived/rescore.json: per hypothesis, the class after the vandkemi fetch, what the fetch supplied, and the tests now runnable.
- **script** — rescore.py. Availability matrix and tests for the nine hypotheses.
- **held** — Section stations data/derived/triage_sections.json. What triage.py counted from the water-chemistry extract: the stations in localities named for the Belts and the Sound that carry all three nutrients, split by locality prefix, with their station numbers.
- **assumption** — A class is a judgement on its blocker. Each class was set by reading the row's blocker against the page's class definitions. Another reader could place a row differently, and the counts are exact counts of these judgements and nothing more. If the definitions were applied differently, every count on the page would move with them.

**Why it follows:** The register's entries for these hypotheses record the monitoring programme without microbial community composition or viral counts, the only Danish viral counts made in a pressure chamber, and the research sequencing found - eelgrass and sediment microbiomes, ARMS and eDNA sampling - with no host condition, exposure, exopolymer production, redox pairing or fungal biomass alongside. The cluster sizes are counted in triage.json and compared by the generator.

**Replaces an earlier claim**, retired on 2026-09-11 to the [archive](ARCHIVE.md#C-TR-OLD-MICROBIAL): Danish research sequencing of marine microbial communities exists outside the monitoring (source register), so 'not one Danish marine station sequences a microbial community, or surveys fungi' overstated the absence, and 'more than any other single absence' rested on no count of the others. The page bounds the absence to the monitoring and compares the clusters it names.

<a id="C-DZ-Z8-P-ART"></a>
### The artefact: the apparent-Kd decline with depth that this project's light analysis measures - the median ratio of lower-half to upper-half Kd rising from its value for profiles starting at the surface to its value for the deepest-starting band - weakens as FDOM rises; the sign is the prediction and the magnitude, which needs an assumed K(λ), is not part of the test.

`C-DZ-Z8-P-ART` · **stipulated** — a rule this project sets itself, with its reason

Said on [hypodrafts/Z8.md](hypodrafts/Z8.md).

**Why it follows:** Dissolved organic matter narrows the spread of K(λ) across the band, and that spread is what produces the decline; light.py computes the ratios by start-depth band.

```mermaid
graph BT
  C-DZ-Z8-P-ART("The artefact: the apparent-Kd decline with depth that this...")
  D-LR-LIGHT[("Light attenuation · data/derived/light.json")]
  X-LR-LIGHT["light.py"]
  A-DZ-CDOM{"Dissolved organic matter · absorbs most in the blue"}
  D-LR-LIGHT --> C-DZ-Z8-P-ART
  X-LR-LIGHT --> C-DZ-Z8-P-ART
  A-DZ-CDOM --> C-DZ-Z8-P-ART
  style C-DZ-Z8-P-ART fill:#173a26,stroke:#3fb950,color:#d7ffe4
  style D-LR-LIGHT fill:#1c4e70,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#e6edf3
  style X-LR-LIGHT fill:#21262d,stroke:#8b949e,color:#c9d1d9
  style A-DZ-CDOM fill:#4a3a12,stroke:#e8a33d,color:#ffeccc,stroke-dasharray:3 2
```

- **held** — Light attenuation data/derived/light.json. Depth reaching the light threshold per cast, its trend over all casts and at stations present at both ends of the record, and by where the cast started.
- **script** — light.py. Fits the profiles and computes the trends and the split by start depth.
- **assumption** — Dissolved organic matter absorbs most in the blue. Absorption by coloured dissolved organic matter rises toward short wavelengths, so more of it removes the blue end of the PAR band near the surface and narrows the spread of K(λ) across the band. The artefact prediction is void if this does not hold in these waters.

**Assessed** — no script computes this. It is a reading or a judgement, assessed by a person.
